theory.title: Reflexionar sobre errores pasados y dar consejos
theory.explanation: Para hablar de acciones pasadas que ahora consideras buenas o malas decisiones, utiliza should have + participio pasado (I should have checked) y shouldn't have + participio pasado (I shouldn't have ignored it). Could have + participio pasado expresa una posibilidad u oportunidad que existía, aunque no se realizara. La estructura es modal + have + past participle; no uses el pasado simple después de have. Para dar consejos actuales, utiliza should + verbo base. Puedes explicar causas con because y consecuencias con so. I regret + -ing expresa arrepentimiento; I wish + past perfect expresa que te gustaría que el pasado hubiera sido diferente.
theory.tip: Distingue el consejo actual del arrepentimiento pasado: You should check (ahora) frente a You should have checked (antes). Después de should/could have siempre va el participio: should have gone, no should have went.

patterns.label: Should have + participio: debería haber
patterns.pattern: Should have + participio pasado para expresar un consejo o una acción que habría sido mejor en el pasado.
examples: I should have listened carefully.
You should have called earlier.

patterns.label: Shouldn't have + participio: no debería haber
patterns.pattern: Shouldn't have + participio pasado expresa que una acción pasada fue una mala idea.
examples: I shouldn't have spent so much money.
He shouldn't have ignored the message.

patterns.label: Could have + participio: podría haber
patterns.pattern: Could have + participio pasado expresa una posibilidad u oportunidad pasada que no se aprovechó.
examples: We could have taken a taxi.
She could have asked the teacher.

patterns.label: Formas negativas
patterns.pattern: Coloca not después de should/could: should not have o could not have.
examples: You shouldn't have lied.
I couldn't have finished without help.

patterns.label: Preguntas con should have
patterns.pattern: Should + sujeto + have + participio para preguntar qué habría sido aconsejable.
examples: Should I have told her the truth?
What should we have done?

patterns.label: Participios pasados
patterns.pattern: Después de have utiliza el participio pasado, no el pasado simple.
examples: I should have gone (no: should have went).
They could have seen it.

patterns.label: Should: dar consejos en presente
patterns.pattern: Should + verbo base sirve para recomendar algo en el presente o futuro.
examples: You should speak to your manager.
We should leave earlier.

patterns.label: Because y so: razón y resultado
patterns.pattern: Because introduce la razón; so introduce el resultado.
examples: I was tired, so I went home.
I apologised because I was wrong.

patterns.label: Primer condicional: posibilidades reales
patterns.pattern: If + present simple, will + verbo base para consecuencias posibles futuras.
examples: If I plan ahead, I'll avoid problems.
If you ask, she'll help.

patterns.label: Reflexión y responsabilidad
patterns.pattern: Usa I regret + -ing, I wish + past perfect y take responsibility para reflexionar.
examples: I regret buying it.
I wish I had checked first.

content.passage: Last month, Daniel made a mistake while organising a community event. He booked a small room without checking how many people had registered. On the evening, more than twice as many guests arrived, and some had to wait outside. Daniel felt embarrassed because he had wanted everything to go well. The event manager helped him find a larger room nearby, but the change caused a delay. Afterwards, Daniel apologised to the guests and took responsibility for the problem. He realised that he should have checked the registration list and could have asked another volunteer to help with the arrangements. He also understood that he shouldn't have assumed that only a few people would come. The manager accepted his apology and praised him for dealing with the situation calmly. Daniel learned an important lesson: good planning means checking details and asking questions when something is unclear. Next time, he will prepare a list, confirm the booking and arrive early.

items.prompt: Describe a mistake you made and what you learned from it.
items.modelAnswer: I once forgot to check the date of an appointment. I arrived a day late and felt embarrassed. I should have written it in my calendar. Since then, I always check important dates.

items.prompt: Talk about something you should have done differently at school.
items.modelAnswer: I should have asked more questions when I didn't understand a topic. I was sometimes too shy, so I missed useful explanations. Now I know that asking for help is important.

items.prompt: Give advice to someone who has spent too much money.
items.modelAnswer: You should make a budget and check your spending every week. You shouldn't buy things just because they are on sale. You could also save a small amount each month.

items.prompt: Describe a time when you apologised to someone.
items.modelAnswer: I once arrived late to meet a friend and didn't send a message. I apologised because I knew I had wasted her time. I should have told her earlier that I was delayed.

items.prompt: What could you have done to avoid a recent problem?
items.modelAnswer: I could have prepared my presentation earlier. I left it until the last evening, so I felt stressed. Next time, I'll divide the work into smaller tasks.

items.prompt: Talk about a warning you should have taken seriously.
items.modelAnswer: I once ignored a warning about heavy rain before a walk. We got very wet and had to return early. I should have checked the forecast and taken suitable clothes.

items.prompt: Explain why blaming others is not always helpful.
items.modelAnswer: Blaming other people doesn't solve a problem. It's better to take responsibility for your part and discuss how to improve. I think people should listen before they judge.

items.prompt: Describe a decision you regret or don't regret.
items.modelAnswer: I don't regret joining a sports club, although I was nervous at first. I could have started earlier, but I learned a lot and met new friends.

items.prompt: Give three pieces of advice to a new student.
items.modelAnswer: You should arrive early, ask questions and make notes. You shouldn't worry about making small mistakes. You could join a club to meet people.

items.prompt: Talk for two minutes about a lesson that changed the way you act.
items.modelAnswer: A lesson I learned was to check details instead of making assumptions. I once organised a group activity and forgot to confirm the time. Several people arrived late. I should have sent a reminder and checked everyone's availability. Since then, I plan ahead and ask for help when I need it.

content.audioTranscript: Maya: How did the presentation go yesterday? Leo: It was fine in the end, but I made a few mistakes. Maya: What happened? Leo: I forgot to save my slides, so I had to use an older version. I should have checked the file before the meeting. Maya: Could you have emailed yourself a copy? Leo: Yes, I could have done that. I also shouldn't have arrived at the last minute because I needed time to test the projector. Maya: Did anyone complain? Leo: No, but I apologised to the team for the delay. Maya: What will you do next time? Leo: I'll prepare everything the day before and ask someone to check the equipment. Maya: That's good advice. We all make mistakes, but we can learn from them.
